thread:
mike: heads-up POC hit a hard stop with ACME SEA lab. They tried to pin redwood-llama-13b@v2.0.0 and get 503s and 404s intermittently. When they ramp concurrency they also see 429s. Need triage + customer-friendly response. cc @sarah @diego

sarah: are they on Private appliance or Dedicated? any request examples/logs?

mike: Private appliance in ap-southeast-1. paste of request below and two log excerpts. customer insists on v2.0.0 for new safety callbacks.

```bash
curl -X POST https://private.acme.example/api/v1/chat \
 -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \
 -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
 -d '{"model":"redwood-llama-13b@v2.0.0","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Generate outline"}]}'
```

logs:
2026-04-05T09:22:11Z ERROR serve.router request_id=def321 code=404 msg="ModelArtifactMissing: redwood-llama-13b@v2.0.0 not found for hw=x86_80g"
2026-04-05T09:22:12Z ERROR runtime.exec request_id=def322 code=503 msg="worker crashed: decoder oom" 
2026-04-05T09:22:13Z WARN  serve.rate request_id=def323 code=429 msg="concurrency throttle: limit=120 active=135"

priya: quick context 13b v2.0.0 artifacts were gated pending license ok from model-licensing team. For on-prem we only shipped v1.9.7 because v2 has a restrictive license that required customer legal sign-off. If their appliance image is older it likely doesn't contain v2 artifacts, hence 404. The 503 may be from an incompatible quant build or unexpected memory profile on their HW.

diego: agree. Also the tokenizer change between 1.9.x and 2.0.0 can cause runtime crashes if the runtime loads mismatched tokenizer files. That explains decoder oom in some runs (mixed artifacts).

ethan: remediation options for POC 
- immediate: ask them to pin redwood-llama-13b@v1.9.7 (artifact present) and test; enable fallback_policy: compatible_variant in client.
- short: if they require v2.0.0 features, we can request signed license addendum and then trigger a private artifact promotion/compile (ETA ~3-6 hours, depends on quant queue and legal sign-off).
- alternate: route only safety-callback calls to Hosted under an egress-limited proxy we control (we can token-scope the calls). Need customer consent + compliance sign-off.

priya: i'll flag the license question in the security packet. @mike can you confirm whether ACME already signed any model-specific licensing addendum?

mike: they said "we reviewed but the legal team hasn't signed the v2 addendum". They're hesitant to open egress for Hosted.

sarah: for the 429s we should also verify agent config: worker_count, max_concurrent_chats, and token_budget. Private defaults are conservative. If they tried bursting to 200 concurrent chats on a single appliance, we'll hit throttle. Two low-risk changes: bump worker_count by 2 and increase max_concurrent_chats in /etc/redwood/agent.conf, then restart agent. Longer term: add a second appliance or Dedicated trial.

build-bot: build queued: redwood-llama-13b@v2.0.0 compile job id=build/1801001255 (triggered by diego). ETA ~4h (quant queue position 7).

priya: compliance note: temporary Hosted routing requires a signed SOC addendum for ACME plus written confirmation of the exact scope of egressed data (we must capture PII policy). I'll draft language for the security questionnaire (Q12/Q13).

mike: sales ask: if we offer a Dedicated micro-trial (2 x A10G equiv) just for the v2 workload, what's a ballpark monthly trial price to present to ACME? we need something quick for procurement.

ethan: back-of-envelope: 2 GPUs reserved ~ $6k/mo list. For a 30 day trial with 8/5 usage we can present ~$2k one-month trial discount option with a short-term commitment. i'll send numbers in DM.

diego: customer-facing message to propose: (1) switch to v1.9.7 to unblock immediately; (2) enable fallback_policy: compatible_variant; (3) if v2 features are required, sign license addendum -> we queue private build (ETA ~4h) or allow limited Hosted proxy for safety callbacks pending legal. include instructions to increase agent worker_count to mitigate 429s.

mike: will send that plan to ACME now. I'll also attach the logs and ask them to run a quick tracer command we use to check artifact presence: 

```bash
# run on appliance
redwood-agent inspect-artifacts | grep llama-13b
```

compliance-bot: reminder: any customer consent for Hosted routing must be recorded in the ticketing system and linked to their security questionnaire. See internal playbook: https://on.redwood/compliance/hosted-proxy-playbook

mike: thanks all. i'll reply to ACME with the three options and ask about license sign-off. ping thread when build completes or if customer wants Dedicated trial. :point_up:
